subject: Privacy & Digital Rights
title: Export Controls on Encryption
description: Learn Export Controls on Encryption in one minute.

hook.text: Until 1996, exporting strong encryption software from the US was legally the same as exporting missiles.

buildup.text: The International Traffic in Arms Regulations classified encryption as a munition alongside tanks and bombs.

discovery.text: Software companies couldn't include strong encryption in products sold overseas, crippling global security.

twist.text: Activists wore t-shirts printed with encryption source code. Customs couldn't arrest someone for wearing a shirt.

climax.text: Export controls were relaxed in 2000. But the debate over who deserves strong encryption continues.

punchline.text: Encryption on a t-shirt. Too absurd to regulate.

quiz.question: How was encryption classified by US law before 2000?
options: As a munition alongside weapons and military equipment
As a consumer product with no restrictions
As an educational tool exempt from regulation
